Setup: I made a fresh copy from the snapshot at f6rework/verify-slot-rule-v2/repo, with data symlinked. The full patch has sha256 ff55e1d0...abec9ad, which matches the stated hash, and applies cleanly with patch -p1. All 5 FROZEN_hashes.txt entries are OK. Its seeds and gold_queries.json are byte-identical to the author's phase-1 output, and build_dataset --check passes. The gold sha256 is a93ca70f...0f25; the design text writes "...0e07", which is a typo borrowed from the __main__.py hash. The rag.py diff has the same +/- lines as the F6 reference diff.

Tests: the full suite passes, 184 passed and 136 subtests, matching the design's report. With my added tests/test_abstention_verifier.py it is 187 passed and 6 xfailed. The known flake did not trigger.

Benchmark test, rerun by me with the official harness: `evaluation.ablation --split test --candidate-limit 20 --abstain-threshold 0.0` in f6rework/verify-slot-rule-v2/out/bench_test_v2. hybrid_full: accepted 99.6% (246/247), refused 17.4% (4/23), balanced 58.5%, grounded 90.4%. This is identical to the design.

External contexts: I re-collected LongMemEval questions 1-100 and LoCoMo conv-26 (199 questions) with the frozen code. Source order, raw logits (max difference 0.0) and v2 decisions are identical on 100/100 and 199/199 rows. Separately, the F6 replay on the designer's contexts matches the F6 verifier's own independently collected numbers (LME 398/470 + 7/30, LoCoMo 1495/1540 + 5/446). So the contexts are faithful.

Labels: checked against the raw data with my own script (tools/indep_check.py). LME has 30 _abs questions in matching order; LoCoMo has 446 category-5 questions; benchmark dev has 7 unanswerables and test has 23. The reranker status is 'applied' on every row, and every source has a float logit.

Replay of all 4 rules on all 5 sets, given as accepted / refused / balanced, reproduces the design table exactly:

| Dev calib | 45/45, 0/45, 50.0% | 36/45, 5/45, 45.6% | 20/45, 10/45, 33.3% | 45/45, 11/45, 62.2% |
| Bench dev | 83/83, 0/7, 50.0% | 83/83, 2/7, 64.3% | 79/83, 3/7, 69.0% | 83/83, 3/7, 71.4% |
| Bench test | 247/247, 0/23, 50.0% | 244/247, 3/23, 55.9% | 235/247, 4/23, 56.3% | 246/247, 4/23, 58.5% |

| LoCoMo | 1540/1540, 0/446, 50.0% | 1495/1540, 5/446, 49.1% | 1440/1540, 23/446, 49.3% | 1516/1540, 7/446, 50.006% |

v2 abstention precision: 100% (calib), 100% (bench dev), 80% (bench test), 22.2% (LME), 22.6% (LoCoMo). Grounded correctness, v2 against no abstention: 90.4% vs 89.3% (bench test), 31.4% vs 31.4% (LME), 16.7% vs 16.5% (LoCoMo).

Hypergeometric test against a random abstainer at the same rate (my addition): bench test p = 0.0002 (real signal), LME p = 0.096 (not significant), LoCoMo p = 0.56 (no signal).

My probes (52 real-store + 47 hand-built context = 99):
- Real store: 30 memories, 50 questions (30 answerable, 20 unanswerable) through hybrid retrieval with the local reranker. False abstentions 2/30; refusals 15/20.
- Hand-built contexts: 47 cases deliberately aimed at the regexes. False abstentions 15/25; refusals 8/22. This failure rate is adversarial by construction and is not a rate estimate.

issues.issue: No meaningful refusal power on either external set, so it fails the adoption rule. LoCoMo balanced is 50.006% (+0.0), and abstention precision 22.6% equals the 22.5% base rate. LME is +2.6 balanced from 2/30 refusals and is not significantly better than random abstention at the same rate. As an opt-in feature it mostly adds about 1.5% false abstentions on conversational data for almost no gain.
issues.evidence: Replay plus re-collection: LME 463/470 accepted, 2/30 refused; LoCoMo 1516/1540, 7/446. Against a random abstainer at the same rate: LME p=0.096, LoCoMo p=0.56. Bench test p=0.0002 is the only significant set, and its unanswerables are of the 'attribute never stated' kind the rule targets.

issues.issue: Real names that collide with the stop or calendar lists are excluded, so a relation-name question false-abstains even though the name is stated next to the relation word. _relation_names filters runs through `excluded`, which includes _STOP ('will', 'may') and _CALENDAR ('june', 'april', 'jan', 'jun', 'may', 'august').
issues.evidence: Each case below returns unfilled_name_slot. Real-store probe: "What's my partner's name?" with memory "My partner Jun is a sound engineer...". Hand-built contexts: "My brother Will is visiting", "My daughter June starts school", "My sister April just got engaged", "My colleague Jan sits next to me". Pinned as expectedFailure in tests/test_abstention_verifier.py.

issues.issue: A relation word used as a possessive modifier turns the question into relation_name, and then only a name adjacent to the relation word counts. A question asking for the name of the relative's shop, pet or similar therefore ignores a correctly stated name.
issues.evidence: Real-store probe: "What's the name of my mum's shop?" with the top source (logit 4.6) "Mum runs a small florist shop in Leiden called Bloemkast." gives unfilled_name_slot. A related anchoring miss: "What is the name of my son's teacher?" with "Mrs. Patel, his teacher, says..." is refused, because the sentence never says 'son'.

tools/probe_synth.py, cases A01-A12, A19, A20 and A24: 15/25 false abstentions on adversarial phrasings. tools/probe_store.py: 2/30 on a clean, well-capitalised store. LoCoMo false abstentions are mostly 'How long did it take...' (8) and 'Which country was X visiting in <date>' (7).

tools/probe_synth.py U02-U10, U14, U21, U22: 14 missed refusals out of 22. Real-store probe: 'Which school did my sister go to?' is answered because of 'Glasgow'; 'How far is the bouldering gym?' is answered because of 'three evenings a week'. The pinned case is 'How long is my yoga class?' with 'I go to yoga twice a week', which returns None.

issues.issue: Coverage gaps by design: who/when/why/which-option/yes-no and computed questions never get a slot. 'Who is my dentist?' or 'When is my mother's birthday?' with no supporting memory is always answered. The design states this; I note it because it caps refusal recall, at 24% on calib.
issues.evidence: question_slot returns None for these (probe U11, U12). Dev calib misses 34/45, including all 6 cross-persona traps.

issues.issue: CLI UX: `ask --abstain` is silently a no-op with the default --generator gemini, and with --no-rerank or a reranker fallback. There is no warning, so a user may believe abstention is active.
issues.evidence: main/__main__.py passes abstain_threshold to answer(), but abstention_reason is called only in the extractive branch, and _slot_evidence returns None unless reranker.status == 'applied'.

issues.issue: Leakage into design is minor and does not move the numbers. The F6 verdict (sanctioned background) quotes 8 held-out LME/LoCoMo questions, and 3 of them appear verbatim in tests/test_abstention.py. The designer probe also uses LoCoMo speaker names (Caroline, Melanie, John), and the F6 verifier's per-question external outputs existed in design/verify-abstention before the freeze. Excluding the 8 quoted questions leaves the results unchanged: LME 459/466 and 2/30; LoCoMo 1513/1536 and 7/446.
issues.evidence: Freeze at 03:30:01 IST (22:00:01Z), before the held-out files (bench 03:37, LME 03:45, LoCoMo 15:22). design/verify-abstention/ext_lme_user.json and ext_locomo.json are timestamped 02:32 and 02:44.

recommended_adjustments:
The design's own conclusion is honest and correct. It fails the default-on adoption rule (+2.6 on LME and +0.0 on LoCoMo, against the required +3 on both). It is not worse than no-abstention on any held-out set. Its answerable acceptance is 98.4% to 99.6% everywhere.

If it ships, ship it only as the patched opt-in: library default None, CLI `ask --abstain`. Make these fixes first (none needs held-out data):

1. Exclude stop and calendar words from relation names only when they are not directly after the relation word, so that "my sister June" and "my brother Will" count.
2. Use relation_name only when the relation word is the head noun ("my sister's name"). For "my mum's shop" or "my brother's dog", fall back to the generic name check.
3. Remove 'a', 'an' and 'half' as standalone number words in _DURATION and _DISTANCE (keep 'half an hour' and the like). Drop the bare `\d+:\d\d` clock-time match.
4. Accept a bare number next to the anchor for money slots ("rent ... 1,450"). Add 'biweekly' and 'bimonthly' to the frequency words.
5. Warn when --abstain is used with gemini or when the reranker did not apply.

Do not claim that the rule detects unanswerable questions in general. It only detects missing typed attributes, and its LoCoMo precision equals the base rate. Any real external gain needs an entity- or premise-aware answerability model, or the LLM generator.

My regression tests documenting the defects are in tests/test_abstention_verifier.py (6 expectedFailure plus 3 safe-property tests).
